scope: Synthetic single-host model; no proprietary HyperFeed code or measured production mix
Identical phased trace, full returned rows and per-phase state/output parity against serial reference
One process per worker, rotating assignments; distinct events ordered per family, duplicate deliveries compete
128 preallocated typed slots/family; native guards before Aerostore snapshot, PostgreSQL FOR UPDATE at transaction start
Aerostore native transactional indexes protect empty predicates and publish with rows; stale indexed snapshots retry explicitly
Aerostore direct shared memory vs PostgreSQL local client/server; not equal transport overhead
WAL enabled, asynchronous acknowledgement in both; clean WAL drain checked, crash durability untested
Native contract probes supply no predicate lock and determine overall compatibility status
No speedup claim: rates include process dispatch/barriers and bounded fixture coordination

cases.name: serializable_absent_candidate_creation
cases.details: Expected one commit and one serialization rejection after overlapping empty candidate searches activate different slots for the same key. Observed initial counts=0/0, committed=1, rejected=1, matching_rows=1, matching_index_postings=1. Native predicate dependencies and automatic index maintenance; no caller-supplied locks.

cases.name: committed_row_and_index_visibility
cases.details: Expected staged writes to remain invisible, and native commit to publish row and index together. Before commit row=Some(10), new_key=[]; immediately after commit row=Some(20), new_key=[0], fresh_reader_committed=true, overlapping_reader_committed=false, raw_old_postings=[], raw_new_postings=[0].

cases.name: index_candidates_respect_transaction_snapshot
cases.details: Expected the old snapshot's row to remain discoverable after a key move, or explicit serialization rejection. Independent witness sees row=Some(10); old_key_candidates=[], rejected_at_lookup=true, candidate_reader_committed=false. Operational errors are not accepted as serialization protection.

cases.name: savepoint_and_whole_message_rollback
cases.details: Expected rollback to preserve pre-savepoint multirow writes [90,60,0], discard nested candidate writes, and leave the committed transfer unchanged after a later whole-message abort. Observed restored=[Some(90), Some(60), Some(0)], committed=true, committed_rows=[(0, 90), (1, 60), (2, 0)], after_abort=[(0, 90), (1, 60), (2, 0)]. This probe covers native table state; it makes no claim about an external index overlay.

cases.name: multirow_table_snapshot_visibility
cases.details: Expected a reader spanning a two-row transfer to retain [100,50] in its snapshot, and a new reader to observe [90,60]. Observed old_reader=[Some(100),Some(50)], writer_committed=true, new_reader=[Some(90), Some(60)], new_reader_committed=true. Both views must conserve total=150.

cases.name: concrete_read_dependency_write_skew
cases.details: Expected one serialization rejection when overlapping transactions read both active records and each deactivates a different record. Observed committed=1, rejected=1, remaining_active=1, final_rows=[(0, 0), (1, 1)]. This contrasts concrete row-read dependencies with the separate empty-candidate probe.
